title: Forecast-driven Pause Scheduler and Resumable Canary Orbit
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a forecasting-led pausepoint scheduler for canary rollouts, snapshot-backed resumable canary lanes, and a single-click snapshot bisect + replay tool for rapid rollback root-cause isolation.
body:
Summary: Implements a forecasting-led 'pausepoint' scheduler that proactively inserts safe holdpoints into staged rollouts when short-term telemetry trends cross configurable thresholds. Introduces resumable canary lanes that persist snapshot checkpoints (request/response contexts + KV cache state) allowing traffic to be frozen, inspected, and replayed for bisecting regressions. Adds a small hedging executor that can bring up lightweight 'safety' replicas to absorb load during an uncertain horizon and a snapshot-bisect tool that replays historical traffic slices to pinpoint the snapshot that introduced a regression.

Motivation and context: Production rollouts at Redwood are conservative but often reactive: teams wait for an SLO breach or alert before stopping a canary. This PR enables predictive intervention by using short-horizon metric forecasts (10-60s window) to open pausepoints earlier and reduce blast radius. Combined with resumable lanes and snapshot-based bisect/replay we reduce time-to-rollback and the need for broad rollbacks across cohorts. Linked: ENG-2749 (pausepoint scheduler design), ENG-2814 (snapshot replay tooling), SUP-9123 (incident that motivated auto-bisect prototype).

What changed (high level): 1) rollout/scheduler: adds ForecastPauseScheduler controller (new CRD-like configmap structure under rollout configs) and associated runtime hooks; 2) checkpointing: persisting light-weight snapshots to object store with deterministic ids and small metadata; 3) hedging lanes: a pluggable lane type that launches small inference workers in a lower-QPS, lower-memory mode to collect guard metrics; 4) bisect tool: CLI endpoint /api/v1/rollouts/<id>/bisect which runs binary search over snapshots and replays sampled traffic to surface the first-failing snapshot; 5) telemetry: new short-horizon forecast metric family (rollout.forecast.delta, rollout.forecast.confidence) and debug tracing for pause events.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler algorithm implemented + unit tests - [x] Snapshot serializer + store adapter (S3-compatible) - [x] Bisect replay harness + integration tests against small canary cluster - [x] Hedging lane runtime and fallback policy - [x] Docs: rollout config guide and troubleshooting - [x] E2E smoke run in benchmark-lab (green) - [x] Backwards compatibility tests for existing rollout configs

Behavioral notes and config examples: The new scheduler uses EWMA + simple AR(1) forecasting on key metrics (p50 latency, error-rate). A pausepoint is scheduled if forecasted error-rate exceeds threshold T within horizon H with confidence C. Example rollout snippet (YAML):

rolloutConfig:
  pausepoint:
    enabled: true
    horizon_seconds: 30
    confidence: 0.8
    thresholds:
      error_rate: 0.01
      p50_latency_ms: 120

Resumable canary lanes persist snapshots every N requests or M seconds (configurable). Snapshots include a light index of affected sessions plus KV-cache token pointers; payloads are compressed to minimize S3 usage. Bisect replay supports deterministic seeds to preserve request ordering semantics for session-coherent workloads.

Files changed (high level): - rollout/controller/scheduler/forecast_pause_scheduler.go (core algorithm + config parsing) - rollout/controller/checkpoint/checkpoint_store.go (S3 adapter + retention policy) - rollout/hedging/executor.go (hedged worker lifecycle) - tooling/bisect/replay_service.go (HTTP handler + replay harness) - docs/rollouts/pause_scheduler.md - tests/integration/bisect_e2e_test.go - sdk/rollouts/client.go (new bisect API surface)

Commit summary: - f2a1b2c: initial forecasting scheduler + unit tests - b3c2d4e: checkpoint store and snapshot format v1 - c4d5e6f: hedging lane runtime and example config - d5e6f7a: bisect replay harness + integration test - e6f7a8b: docs and release notes - f7a8b9c: CI fixes and flake handles

Review thread (highlights): - Jordan Kim (reviewer): "Algorithm looks sound; can we document when we expect false positives from the AR(1) model and provide an opt-out?"
  Asha: "Added explicit confidence param and opted default to 0.8; added docs section on model limitations and suggested production guide."

- Priya Menon (SRE): "Concern about snapshot retention and cost — what's default TTL?"
  Asha: "Default retention set to 24h and max total storage per rollout capped; made both configurable and added cleanup job. We also sample snapshots by rate to control growth."

- Ethan Zhao (runtime): "Hedging lane allocates smaller memory; make sure quantized model variants are used there to bound OOM risk."
  Asha: "Hedging executor now prefers quantized variants and will fall back to CPU-promo instances if GPU capacity is low."

CI checks: - unit: pass - integration: pass (bisect E2E green in benchmark-lab) - lint: pass - load tests: informational run (no regressions observed)

Performance/regressions: Local performance microbenchmarks show a median 1.3% overhead for coordinator loops when pausepoint is enabled (cold path), hedging lanes add negligible impact to main plane since they run on separate nodes. Snapshot storage amortized to ~2.6MB/hour per active canary at default sampling rate.

Operational playbook (short): - When a pausepoint opens, the rollout is paused and annotated with forecast reason + snapshot id. - Operators can invoke bisect endpoint to run an automated binary search — the tool replies with the first-failing snapshot id and an optional replay artifact for local debugging. - If rollback is required, a single-click rollback will revert to the previous stable snapshot and optionally trigger an automated remedial canary with hedging lane enabled.

Migration and compatibility: Existing rollouts without pausepoint config are unaffected. The new code paths are gated behind the rollout.pausepoint.enabled flag. SDK changes are additive: new bisect client method and rollout introspection fields.

Security and cost controls: Snapshots are encrypted server-side when uploaded to S3 and access is restricted by rollout-id-scoped IAM policies. Snapshot retention TTL and per-rollout storage caps are configurable at org-level.

Merge outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-11-10 after two approvals (Jordan Kim, Priya Menon). No post-merge CI regressions observed.

Follow-ups (planned): - ENG-2901: add a multivariate forecast model (seasonal/local-trend) for less noisy signals - ENG-2902: UI surface in Console for pausepoint inspection and bisect results - ENG-2903: tighter snapshot dedup and delta-compression to reduce storage usage
